record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For the NP-hard cases of deciding whether a target matching is reachable from an initial matching, and of finding a Pareto-optimal matching, in house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine whether these hard cases become tractable under useful parameters and develop a parameterized complexity theory for them.

evidence.quote: Also, the hard cases in Theorems 5 and 6 could be tackled from a parameterised complexity viewpoint.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following house allocation model with exchanges over a social network. There is a set of agents $A = \{a_1,\dots,a_n\}$ and a set of houses $H = \{h_1,\dots,h_n\}$. Each agent $a_i$ has a (possibly weak) preference order $\succeq_i$ over $H$. The social network is an undirected graph $G=(A,E)$ on the agents. A matching is a bijection $M: A \to H$. From a matching $M$, a swap between two adjacent agents $a_i, a_j$ (with $\{a_i,a_j\}\in E$) produces a new matching $M'$ in which $a_i$ and $a_j$ exchange their houses; the swap is allowed only if it is rational/Pareto-improving (each of $a_i, a_j$ weakly prefers the new house and at least one strictly prefers it). A matching $M^*$ is reachable from an initial matching $M_0$ if there is a finite sequence of allowed swaps transforming $M_0$ into $M^*$. A matching $M$ is Pareto-optimal if no other matching $M'$ is weakly preferred by all agents and strictly preferred by at least one.

The following two decision problems are known to be NP-hard in general:
(R) Given $(A,H,G,(\succeq_i)_{i\in A}, M_0, M^*)$, decide whether $M^*$ is reachable from $M_0$ by a sequence of allowed swaps along edges of $G$.
(P) Given $(A,H,G,(\succeq_i)_{i\in A}, M_0)$, find a Pareto-optimal matching reachable from $M_0$ (or decide existence of one with prescribed properties).

Identify natural structural or numerical parameters $k$ (e.g., treewidth of $G$, maximum degree, number of distinct preference profiles, number of houses any agent finds acceptable, size of symmetric difference between $M_0$ and $M^*$, etc.) under which these problems admit fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms with running time $f(k)\cdot \mathrm{poly}(n)$, and develop a parameterized complexity theory (FPT algorithms, $W[1]$/$W[2]$-hardness, kernelization lower and upper bounds) classifying the complexity of (R) and (P) with respect to these parameters.
artifact.category_tag: parameterized complexity of matchings under preferences
artifact.status_search_result: Follow-up work has addressed parts of this program. The MFCS 2021 paper "Maximum Votes Pareto-Efficient Allocations via Swaps on a Social Network" and subsequent works refine the complexity landscape of Pareto-efficient swap matchings on social networks (giving polynomial algorithms for path networks with strict preferences and NP-hardness for star networks with weak preferences). Parameterized complexity has been examined for related house-allocation problems (e.g., with lower/upper quotas), but a comprehensive parameterized complexity theory for the specific NP-hard cases of reachability and Pareto-optimality in the social-network swap model does not yet appear to be complete; the broader program remains partially open.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Votes Pareto-Efficient Allocations via Swaps on a Social Network
status_evidence.snippet: Studies complexity of reaching Pareto-efficient matching maximizing number of agents who prefer their match to initial endowment, with polynomial algorithms and NP-hardness depending on network structure.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the complexity of Pareto-optimal swap matchings in social networks.

status_evidence.title: Pareto optimal and popular house allocation with lower and upper quotas
status_evidence.snippet: Parameterized complexity results for Pareto optimal and popular house allocation problems with quotas.
status_evidence.claim: Parameterized complexity has been investigated in related house allocation settings.
